- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥1.0) over recent days, model tends to underpredict upward moves; increase forecast slightly above recent mean.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.0) or mixed, model often overpredicts downward moves; reduce forecast slightly below recent mean.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp upward spikes in sentiment; cap forecast at +10% above recent peak for 3–5 days.
- Model underestimates mean reversion in volatile periods; add 5–10% buffer to forecast if sentiment shifts from bullish to neutral.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to lag by 1–2 days in capturing sentiment-driven momentum; adjust forecast up by 1–2% if sentiment turns bullish within last 3 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes followed by recovery, model often fails to anticipate rebound; add 3–5% upward correction in 3–7 day horizon.
